question: Should this PR intentionally tighten byte-size config validation so unsafe numeric byte counts are rejected instead of rounded on upgrade?
rationale: Root policy treats stricter config validation as compatibility-sensitive; the code fix appears correct, but automation should not silently accept the upgrade behavior for existing malformed configs.

options.title: Accept safe-integer validation
options.body: Merge the focused hardening and document in release context that unsafe byte-size values above JavaScript's safe integer range are now rejected.

options.title: Preserve upgrade tolerance
options.body: Ask for a compatibility mode, warning, or doctor migration if maintainers want existing unsafe numeric configs to keep loading during upgrade.

options.title: Pause for config policy
options.body: Hold the PR until a config owner decides whether malformed but previously accepted byte sizes should fail closed.

recommendation.title: Accept safe-integer validation
recommendation.body: Merge the focused hardening and document in release context that unsafe byte-size values above JavaScript's safe integer range are now rejected.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the shared config byte-size helper and safe-duration precedent this change follows.
